title: Aging‐Induced Ductile‐Brittle‐Ductile Transition in High‐Entropy Alloys and its Implications

recollection.starting_material: Likely a face-centered cubic (FCC) high-entropy alloy such as the equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi system or a derivative multicomponent FCC HEA.
recollection.intervention: Thermal aging/annealing at intermediate temperatures for various times to induce nanoscale precipitation or phase separation.
recollection.structure: Formation first of coherent L1₂-type or B2-type nanoprecipitates that initially strengthen and embrittle the matrix, followed by coarsening or transformation of these precipitates (or recovery/twinning of the matrix) that restores ductility; overall giving a ductile→brittle→ductile sequence as aging proceeds.
recollection.mechanism: Competition between solid-solution–strengthened FCC matrix plasticity, precipitate-shearing or bypass mechanisms, and stress concentrations at semi-coherent interfaces; early stage fine precipitates impede dislocation motion and raise strength but promote cleavage or limited micro-shear banding (brittle behavior), while later-stage coarsened or transformed precipitates allow dislocation-mediated plasticity or nanotwinning, thus re-establishing ductility.
recollection.results: Probably reported yield strength rising from ~450 MPa (solution-annealed) to >800 MPa after moderate aging, with fracture strain dropping from ~50 % to <5 % (brittle regime) and then recovering to ~30 % after prolonged aging; accompanying hardness peak and subsequent decline. These numbers are speculative guesses.

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies intermediate-temperature aging and partially anticipates L1₂ ordering and interface-related stress concentrations, but it misidentifies the starting alloy and treats the evolution mainly as precipitate formation/coarsening. It misses the key jagged B2/FCC boundaries, elevated APBE and modulus, restricted cross-slip, and ductile transition zones. The guessed strength and strain values are unsupported, and the important 600°C and 750°C conditions are absent.
